opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grant varies by category: £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions; Acquisitions and Collections; Long-Term Research), £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications), £2,500 (Research and Travel)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating non-profit for at least 12 months); individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category only. Applications must be predominantly focused on sculpture.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions), Acquisitions and Collections (acquisition, conservation, cataloguing, display), Conferences, Lectures and Publications, Long-Term Research, and Research and Travel (for individuals). Applications considered four times per year; Autumn round currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses (UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and established scholars working on sculpture (Visiting Research, Artist Research and Senior Fellowship types).
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using research facilities at the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence. Applications for 2026/27 are closed; next round of applications opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize (BA and MA each) plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover price value of £50

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines at UK universities, for dissertations submitted within the past academic year relating directly to sculpture.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, with a strong focus on primary and secondary sources and original research. Winning dissertations are added to the Henry Moore Institute Research Library. Submissions for the next prize open in autumn.
